newsitem.title: USA: Successories gets credit pact, closes placement.
newsitem.headline: Successories gets credit pact, closes placement.

text.p: Successories Inc, which reported a profitable third fiscal quarter, said Wednesday it has completed a private placement of $5 million of preferred stock to an investor group and entered into a new credit agreement with its existing lender.

Successories also said it did not recognize any income tax benefit from operating loss carryforwards in the third quarter but does expect to use a significant portion of its remaining carryforward in the fourth quarter of this year.
Successories, a specialty retailer and catalog firm, makes and markets products for business and personal motivation.

The company reported a profit for its fiscal third quarter ended November 30, 1996 of $25,000 compared with a loss of $596,000 in the same quarter a year ago. Fiscal third quarter revenues rose to $14.2 million from $10.8 million last year.

Results benefited from a decline in some expenses and improved efficiencies, the company said. Interest expense rose due to increased borrowings to support a higher level of sales as the company moves into the holiday selling season.

The company said it has completed negotiation of a new long-term credit agreement with its lender. It also has reduced the balance of its term loan with the proceeds of a private equity placement by $4.0 million to $4.5 million while extending the term of the loan into 1998.
Successories also said its line of credit for working capital purposes increased to $4 million from $2.5 million.

The company received $5 million in proceeds from the sale of convertible preferred stock to Infinity Investors Ltd and Seacrest Capital Ltd, private investor groups managed by Clark Hunt of Dallas, Texas. The preferred stock is convertible to common shares beginning 60 days after the closing of the transaction. Proceeds will be used to reduce debt and provide additional working capital to fund growth.
